rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meyte means an animal that died without ritual slaughter, the legal opposite of a properly slaughtered animal, rather than simply anything dead or dying without an external cause.
rows.anchor: “Meyte” canlı mukabili ölü demek değil, hiçbir te’sîr-i hâricî olmadan ölen demek de değil, mezbuh mukabili ölü

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later exception for what is slaughtered establishes that carrion is specifically the opposite of ritually purified meat.
rows.anchor: ki aşağıda gelecek olan إِلَّا مَا ذَكَّيْتُمْ bu tekābülü gösterecektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blood means flowing blood, as clarified in Sūrat al-Anʿām; carrion and blood are intrinsically impure and forbidden, and retained blood partly contributes to carrion's prohibition.
rows.anchor: “Dem”, yani kan ki murad dem-i mesfuh olduğu diğer bir yerde, ezcümle Sûre-i En‘âm’da mübeyyendir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some polytheists defended eating carrion by asking why they could eat animals they killed but not animals killed by God.
rows.anchor: “kendi öldürdüğünüzü [1557] yiyorsunuz da Allah’ın öldürdüğünü niçin yemiyorsunuz?” derlermiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some also filled intestines with blood, roasted them, and served them to guests.
rows.anchor: Kezâlik kanı bağırsaklara doldururlar ve kızartır, misafirlerine yedirirlermiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pig itself is intrinsically impure, as stated in 6:145, so its flesh is forbidden in itself.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i En‘âm’da فَاِنَّهُ رِجْسٌ [6/145] buyurulduğu üzere domuzun kendisi aynen necistir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says pig flesh rather than simply pig because no slaughter exception below can apply to a pig.
rows.anchor: burada وَالخِْنْزِيرِ denilmeyip de وَلَحْمُ ٱلْخِنزِيرِ denilmesi aşağıdaki tezkiye istisnâsına bunun hiç ta‘alluku olamayacağını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An animal slaughtered in another's name, such as invoking al-ʿUzzā, is forbidden whether or not God's name is also invoked.
rows.anchor: denilen” ki beraberinde “bismillah” gerek denilsin gerek denilmesin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Slaughtering for another is a grave injustice and shirk because God created and subjected the animal and granted the right and power to slaughter it; such meat is spiritually and legally carrion.
rows.anchor: o hayvanı Allah’tan başkasının nâmına kesmek bir zulm-i azîm, bir şirktir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These four prohibitions are foundational categories that encompass what follows, which is why many verses mention only them.
rows.anchor: Bu dört esastır. Bundan sonrakiler şer‘an bunların şümûlünde dâhildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pre-Islamic Arabs sometimes treated carrion only as an animal that died spontaneously without an external cause, and ate other carrion types accordingly.
rows.anchor: meyteyi bir te’sîr-i hâricî olmaksızın kendi kendine ölen diye telakkī ederler ve hakikatte meyte kabîlinden olan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-munkhaniqa is an animal suffocated by a rope, noose, hand, or being trapped between objects, or by any other obstruction of breath.
rows.anchor: herhangi bir suretle nefesi tıkanarak boğulup ölen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mawqūdha is an animal struck by a blow from near or far and killed by it.
rows.anchor: yakından veya uzaktan herhangi bir darbe ile vurulup ölmüş olan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mutaraddiya is an animal that falls from a height, into a well, or into water and dies.
rows.anchor: yüksekten aşağı veya bir kuyuya, bir suya düşüp helâk olan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-natīha is an animal that has butted or been butted; an animal killed by a horse's or another animal's kick also fits, though it was already included among the struck animals.
rows.anchor: süsülmüş ve süsmüş olan. At veya diğer bir hayvan çiftesiyle ölen de bu mânada olmakla beraber daha evvel mevkūzede dâhildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What a predator eats means an animal killed or torn by it, specifically its remnant or wounded portion rather than what it has swallowed.
rows.anchor: Belli ki bundan maksad hayvanın boğazına giden değil, artığı ve hatta yırttığıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sebuʿ denotes attacking, seizing predators with fangs, such as lions, tigers, wolves, and dogs; predatory birds with claws are included too.
rows.anchor: “Sebu‘”; “nâb” tâbir olunur sivri dişleri bulunan arslan, kaplan, kurt, köpek vesâire gibi âdeten saldırır, kapar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Turkish, canavar once broadly meant any living animal and could mean pig or wolf, but its ordinary core meaning is a predator that attacks living beings, corresponding to sebuʿ.
rows.anchor: örfümüzde canavarın asıl mânası budur, sebu‘da bu demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some pre-Islamic carrion-eaters and contemporary Christians treat animals killed by strangling, blows, falls, butting, or predators as slaughter-like because an external agent killed them; the author says they remain carrion because they were not slaughtered and drained of blood.
rows.anchor: Hâlbuki bunların beşi de zebh ile kanları akıtılmamış olduğundan tamamen meytedirler ve haramdırlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In his rendering of 5:4, the author calls lawful foods wholesome, describes trained hunting animals as taught from God's teaching, and says to eat what they bring and invoke God's name over it.
rows.anchor: De ki sizin için bütün pâk nimetler helâl kılındı, alıştırarak ve Allah’ın size öğrettiğinden öğreterek yetiştirdiğiniz avcı hayvanların

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His rendering of 5:5 says the foods of the People of the Book and Muslims are lawful to each other.
rows.anchor: kendilerine kitap verilen ümmetlerin taâmları size helâl, sizin taâmlarınız da onlara helâl

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His rendering permits free Muslim women and free women from earlier scriptural communities in marriage when dowries are paid and chastity is kept, without fornication or secret partners.
rows.anchor: kitap verilen ümmetlerin hür kadınları da iffetlerinizi muhafaza ederek, zina etmeksizin, gizli dost tutmaksızın kendilerine mehirlerini verip nikâhladığınız takdirde size helâldir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His rendering says whoever rejects the law's rulings has all deeds annulled and is among the losers in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: her kim şeriatın ahkâmını tanımazsa her hâlde bütün işlediği hederdir ve âhirette o hüsranda kalanlardandır

rows.speaker: İkrime ve Muhammed b. Ka‘b
rows.claim: They report that after Gabriel said angels would not enter a house with a dog, the Prophet ordered dogs killed; after Abu Rafi killed Medina's dogs through al-ʿAwālī, three men asked what was lawful and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: İkrime ve Muhammed b. Ka‘b’den nakledildiğine göre Cebrâil aleyhisselâm “biz kelb bulunan eve girmeyiz” demiş olduğundan dolayı Hazret-i Peygamber köpeklerin öldürülmesini emretmiş

rows.speaker: Ebû Râfi‘
rows.claim: In a report cited with its chain from al-Hākim's Ṣaḥīḥ, Abu Rafi says the Prophet ordered him to kill dogs, after which people asked what had been made lawful from the community he ordered killed and God revealed the verses.
rows.anchor: Hâkim Ebû Abdullah’ın Sahîh’inde senediyle rivayet ettiği üzere Ebû Râfi‘demiştir ki: “Resûlullah bana köpeklerin katlini emretti

rows.speaker: Sa‘îd b. Cübeyr
rows.claim: He reports that ʿAdiyy b. Ḥātim and Zayd al-Khayl asked about dogs and falcons catching game, since some animals survived for slaughter while others died before it; the verse was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: Sa‘îd b. Cübeyr demiştir ki: “Adiyy b. Hâtim ve Zeydü’l- Hayl ‘yâ Resûlallah, biz kelblerle ve doğanlarla av avlarız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the latter report, the question follows from the slaughter exception in 5:3, and the answer explains the legal meaning of ritual slaughter, fitting the context.
rows.anchor: cevap da tezkiyenin ma‘nâ-yı şer‘îsini tafsil ve îzah sadedinde vârid olmuş demek olur ki siyâka pek münâsibdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two reports imply different revelation sequences, one before and one after the prohibition passage, creating a chronology problem if the related 'today' statements refer to separate days.
rows.anchor: Evvelki rivayet bu âyetlerin nüzûlü hurmet âyetinden mukaddem olduğuna, ikinci rivayet de muahhar bulunduğuna delâlet etmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He holds that the several 'today' statements belong to the same period, not separate days; they encompass the final years of the Prophet and make the prohibitions and permissions historically or legally connected.
rows.anchor: bunlar mücerred yevm-i arefeyi değil, Sûre-i Mâide’nin bütün zamân-ı nüzûlünü istî‘âb eden sinîn-i ahîre-i Muhammediyeyi zamân-ı vâhid olarak ifade etmekte

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'they ask you what is lawful for them' can present a general possible question, not only narrate a question that happened at one historical moment.
rows.anchor: sual vâki‘i hikaye değil, “sorarlar” diye vâki‘ve mümkine şâmil olarak daha umûmî bir sual tasavvur edilmek lâzım gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tayyibāt contrasts with impure things; 7:157 says God makes wholesome things lawful and vile things forbidden, so the Muslim table should contain clean, pleasant foods.
rows.anchor: nitekim وَيُحِلُّ لَهُمُ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ وَيُحَرِّمُ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْخَبَٰٓئِثَ [el-A‘râf 7/157]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lexically, tayyib means something enjoyable, clean, and pleasant; by analogy, permitted food free of a presumption of prohibition is also called tayyib because it is harmless.
rows.anchor: “tayyib” lügatta “müstelez”, yani hazzedilen temiz ve hoş şey demektir

rows.speaker: İbn Cerîr Taberî
rows.claim: Tabari and some exegetes gloss tayyibāt as simply lawful things, but the author rejects this as a weakly redundant reading, 'lawful things were made lawful.'
rows.anchor: İbn Cerîr Taberî gibi bazı müfessirîn burada “tayyibât”ı helâller diye tefsir etmişlerse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority of exegetes and jurists take tayyibāt to mean clean, pleasant things that people find appetizing, which the author adopts.
rows.anchor: ekser müfessirîn ve müctehidîn bunun “lezzet ve iştihâ hissedilen temiz ve hoş şeyler” mânasına hamli vâcib [1574] olduğunu göstermişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not every personally liked thing is lawful: corrupted habits and morals do not count, and the criterion is what sound human nature finds clean and agreeable.
rows.anchor: İbret, tab‘-ı selîmedir. Ve tayyibât ancak tab‘-ı selîm erbâbının tiksinmeyip hoşlandıkları şeylerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Desert inhabitants and people under necessity may enjoy eating every kind of animal, but their tastes do not determine what counts as wholesome.
rows.anchor: bâdiye halkı ve ıztırar içinde yaşayanlar her nevi hayvânâtı hoşlanıp yiyebilirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although 2:29 indicates original permissibility and would broadly allow benefiting from earthly things, 7:157 excludes vile things and limits lawful consumption to wholesome goods; absent specific evidence, this is the general rule for determining halal and haram.
rows.anchor: Gerçi خَلَقَ لَكُم مَّا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًۭا [el-Bakara 2/29] medlûlünce ibâha asıldır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pre-Islamic Arabs superstitiously prohibited some otherwise wholesome livestock as bahīra, sāʾiba, waṣīla, and ḥām; 7:32 reinforces that wholesome provision is lawful and helps explain the revelation's purpose.
rows.anchor: tayyibâttan olan en‘âmdan bazılarını Sûre-i En‘âm’da beyan olunacağı üzere “bahîre”, “sâibe”, “vasîle”, “hâm” nâmlarıyla kendilerine tahrim ederler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tayyibāt includes wholesome birds as well as livestock and all plants.
rows.anchor: bu tayyibâtta behîme-i en‘âmdan başka kuşların ve hatta bütün nebâtâtın dahi hoşları dâhildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not imply that every part of an otherwise lawful animal is lawful; impure parts remain forbidden even in animals that were properly slaughtered.
rows.anchor: müzekkâ olan hayvânâtın eczâsı meyânında bulunan habâisin de haram olduğunu iş‘âr etmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In sum, everything that sound nature and sound human disposition find wholesome is lawful.
rows.anchor: Velhâsıl tab‘-ı selîmin ve fıtrat-ı sahîhanın hoşlandığı bütün tayyibât helâl kılındı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cevāriḥ is the plural of jāriḥa, from jarḥ; by association with making an impact it means earners, and can name both limbs that wound or acquire and hunting predators or birds.
rows.anchor: “Cevârih”, “câriha”nın cem‘idir ki esasen “cerh”ten me’huz olup tesir mânası mülâhazasıyla kâsibe mânasına isim olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukallibīn means trainers who accustom hunting animals to pursue prey and teach them hunting.
rows.anchor: “Mükellib” teklîb eden, yani hayvânât-ı cârihayı ava dadandırıp alıştıran, avcılık tâlim edip öğreten demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A trained dog goes when sent, answers a call, holds prey without eating it, does not flee when the owner approaches, obeys restraint, and has made this a habit through at least three repetitions.
rows.anchor: bir kelb, sâhibi tarafından kışkırtıldığı yere gider, çağırılınca icâbet eder, avı tutunca hapseder yemez, sâhibi almak isteyince kaçmaz

rows.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
rows.claim: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal considers two successful repetitions sufficient for a hunting animal to count as trained.
rows.anchor: Ahmed b. Hanbel ikiyi, Hasan-ı Basrî biri kâfi görmüştür

rows.speaker: حسن-ı Basrî
rows.claim: Ḥasan al-Baṣrī considers one successful repetition sufficient for a hunting animal to count as trained.
rows.anchor: Ahmed b. Hanbel ikiyi, Hasan-ı Basrî biri kâfi görmüştür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term taklīb is used by predominance because dogs are the most commonly trained hunters, though kelb may refer to any predatory animal.
rows.anchor: Bu tâlime “teklib” denilmesi tağlib tarîkiyledir. Zira ale’l-ekser tâlim edilen kelblerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To show that kelb is not limited to dogs, he cites the Prophet's prayer that God send one of His kelbs against ʿUtba, whom a lion later ate on the road.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah “اللهمّ سل ِّط عليه كلبًا من كلابك: İlâhî buna kelblerinden bir kelbi musallat et” diye dua etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lawful trained hunters include dogs and other predators, trained through understanding God taught people; they may be kept and bought or sold, but the animals themselves are not food.
rows.anchor: ava alıştırarak Allah’ın size öğrettiği idrâkâttan tâlim ederek öğrettiğiniz mu‘allem avcı hayvanlar helâl kılındı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax says eat from what hunting animals hold, not everything they hold, so one should eat the wholesome portions rather than all parts.
rows.anchor: değil مِمَّآ أَمْسَكْنَ’dir. Tuttuklarının hepsini değil, bir kısmını, eczâ-yı tayyibesini yiyiniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The animals must hold prey for their human owner; prey held for themselves is not covered by the wording.
rows.anchor: mutlaka أَمْسَكْنَ değil أَمْسَكْنَ عَلَيْكُمْ’dür, yani kendilerine değil size tutuverdiklerini yiyiniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a trained dog sent by a hunter wounds and kills prey and the hunter arrives after it is dead, the game is lawful; the trained predator's wound takes the place of ritual slaughter.
rows.anchor: Şu hâlde bir kelb mu‘allem olursa ve avcı tarafından sevk edilir de bir avı tutar, cerh eder, öldürür de avcı ona ölmüş olduğu hâlde yetişirse helâldir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same rule applies to other trained hunting animals and to arrows, spears, and guns; the hunter need not reach the animal alive, since that would erase the distinction between trained and untrained hunters.
rows.anchor: Diğer cevârih ve kezâlik ok, mızrak, tüfek de böyledir. Behemehâl diri iken yetişilip zebh edilmesi şart değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wounding is required: although some permit prey killed by choking or impact based on the wording's apparent generality, the author says such prey is like strangled or struck carrion and forbidden.
rows.anchor: bazıları مِمَّآ أَمْسَكْنَ عَلَيْكُمْ zâhiren mutlaktır diyerek yine yenir demiş ise de doğrusu bunun münhanika veya mevkūzeden farkı yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a trained dog wounds and kills the prey but eats some, the animal is forbidden because it held the prey for itself rather than for its owner.
rows.anchor: kelb-i mu‘allem cerh ü katletmiş olmakla beraber biraz da yemiş bulunursa bu da yenmez. Çünkü o onu kendine tutmuş demektir

rows.speaker: سلمان-ı Fârisî، سعد ب. أبي وقاص، ابن عمر، أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Salman al-Farisi, Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas, Ibn ʿUmar, and Abu Hurayra are each reported to allow eating game that the trained dog has partly eaten.
rows.anchor: Selmân-ı Fârisî’den, Sa‘d b. Ebî Vakkâs’dan, İbn Ömer’den, Ebû Hureyre’den yenir diye rivayet de edilmiştir

rows.speaker: Mâlik ve Evzâî
rows.claim: Malik and al-Awzaʿi also hold that game partly eaten by a trained dog is lawful.
rows.anchor: Mâlik ve Evzâî yenir demişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The issue distinguishes dogs from birds: a bird's eating part of its prey does not bar permissibility, a position held by the Hanafis.
rows.anchor: kuşun yemiş olması hılline mâni‘olmayacağı gösterilmiştir ki Hanefiyye buna kāildirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God's name over the catch means saying the basmala when releasing the dog or bird.
rows.anchor: yani kelbi ve kuşu salarken besmele çekin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God reckons swiftly, people should guard against disobeying His commands.
rows.anchor: ve her hâlde Allah serî‘u’l-hisâb olduğundan emirlerine muhalefetten sakının

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After reinforcing the prohibitions with the statement of perfected religion in 5:3, the passage reaffirms and then generalizes lawful foods.
rows.anchor: Bugün size bütün tayyibât, her nevi hoş nimetler helâl kılındı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Food of the People of the Book is lawful to Muslims, and Muslim food to them; the author includes slaughtered and hunted foods, bread, and other foods, which Muslims may serve or sell to them.
rows.anchor: bir de ehl-i kitâbın taâmı, yani gerek bu tayyibâttan kestikleri ve avladıkları ve gerek ekmek vesâire gibi mat‘ûmâtları size helâl

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three views define the People of the Book's food: their slaughtered meat; bread, fruit, and foods not requiring slaughter, attributed to Zaydiyya imams; or all foods including slaughtered meat.
rows.anchor: “Taâm”dan murad ne olduğu hakkında üç vecih vardır: Birincisi zebîha demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most exegetes prefer the first definition, slaughtered meat, because other foods are not specific to their makers, whereas slaughter becomes food through the slaughterer's act and its attribution to the People of the Book is meaningful.
rows.anchor: Ekseriyet evvelki vechi tercih etmişlerdir. Çünkü zebîhadan mâ‘adâsının taâm olmasında sâhibine ihtisâsı yoktur
